title: Beyond Static Vision: Scene Dynamic Field Unlocks Intuitive Physics Understanding in Multi-modal Large Language Models
claim: Existing benchmarks entangle many capabilities and leave models far below humans; isolating low-level tasks and adding simulator-driven training closes the gap and transfers.
layout: 3 panels: left gray prior panel, right top blue task panel, right bottom orange method panel; bar charts and transfer arrow
description: The figure has three rounded panels. The gray left panel, titled 'Existing Benchmarks', shows a stick-and-fluid puzzle photo with a multiple-choice question. Below it is a bar chart of four MLLMs' accuracy (about 34–42%) against a dashed human line at 72.67, marked 'Huge Gap'. Beside the chart, arrows from four entangled abilities (physical common sense, dynamic perception, temporal-spatial reasoning, logical inference) point to a flask icon. The blue top-right panel, 'Low-Level Tasks', shows the two tasks. Next Frame Selection uses oil-splash frames with four candidate images and a green check. Temporal Coherence Verification uses milk-pouring frames with one red-dotted unnatural frame and a yes/no question. The orange bottom-right panel, 'Scene Dynamic Field', shows simulated cup frames and a simulator-style render. Two bar charts show SDF-Ours winning on the fluid NFS task and on a transferred smoke task. Icons for sand, plasticine, cloth and smoke mark the unseen domains.
caption: Existing benchmarks entangle multiple capabilities, leading to poor performance in SOTA MLLMs. To address this, we introduce two low-level tasks to assess intuitive physics understanding: Next Frame Selection and Temporal Coherence Verification. Our proposed Scene Dynamic Field (SDF) directly enhances MLLMs' dynamic understanding and shows strong generalization.
abstract: While Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in image and video understanding, their ability to comprehend the physical world has become an increasingly important research focus. Despite their improvements, current MLLMs struggle significantly with high-level physics reasoning. In this work, we investigate the first step of physical reasoning, i.e., intuitive physics understanding, revealing substantial limitations in understanding the dynamics of continuum objects. To isolate and evaluate this specific capability, we introduce two fundamental benchmark tasks: Next Frame Selection (NFS) and Temporal Coherence Verification (TCV). Our experiments demonstrate that even state-of-the-art MLLMs perform poorly on these foundational tasks. To address this limitation, we propose Scene Dynamic Field (SDF), a concise approach that leverages physics simulators within a multi-task fine-tuning framework. SDF substantially improves performance, achieving up to 20.7% gains on fluid tasks while showing strong generalization to unseen physical domains. This work not only highlights a critical gap in current MLLMs but also presents a promising cost-efficient approach for developing more physically grounded MLLMs. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/andylinx/Scene-Dynamic-Field.
